The pilot phase is officially over.

Writer CEO May Habib told Bloomberg this week that enterprise AI's biggest hurdle has shifted. It is no longer about proving AI works in a controlled experiment. It is about changing how companies are organized to use it.

This is the gap that separates companies getting real returns from AI and companies collecting successful proof-of-concepts that never scale. The technology is not the bottleneck anymore. The org chart is.

AI orchestration — connecting agents, workflows, data, and people into unified systems — is becoming the framework for this next phase. It is not about buying a new platform. It is about redesigning how decisions get made, how data flows, and how teams collaborate when AI is a core operating capability.

The executives who will lead from here are not the ones running the most experiments. They are the ones willing to reorganize around what those experiments proved.
